newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA SPOIL JUVE'S CHANCES OF GOING TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA SPOIL JUVE'S CHANCES OF GOING TOP.

text.p: Defender Massimo Beghetto, who had spent his career toiling in lower divisions until this season, ended Juventus's unbeaten serie A record on Sunday by scoring the winner in a 2-1 victory for Vicenza.
The surprise result left Inter alone at the top on 11 points, ahead of four clubs including Juventus on 10. Inter are now the only unbeaten club in Italian soccer.

Apart from ruining the European Cup holders' chances of returning to the top of the league, the 71st-minute strike will also have raised the hopes of Turkish club Fenerbahce who meet Juventus in a Champions' League clash on Wednesday.

Beghetto's goal, his second of the season, came after Ciro Ferrara appeared to have claimed a point for the visitors with a 47th-minute headed equaliser to Uruguayan Marcelo Otero's opening goal in the 19th minute.
Juventus finished the match with 10 men after midfielder Alessio Tacchinardi was sent off for a crude tackle.
Inter were 2-0 winners over Piacenza on Saturday despite having only 10 men for much of the match after England midfielder Paul Ince was sent off.
Roma beat Milan 3-0 at the Olympic stadium on Saturday for the first time in 11 years to go ahead of Bologna, Parma and Juventus.

Despite missing first-team regulars Alessandro Del Piero and Antonio Conte with injuries as well as the suspended Alen Boksic, Juventus manager Marcello Lippi blamed poor finishing for the defeat at Vicenza.
Both Vladimir Jugovic in the first half and, most crucial of all, Michele Padovano with two minutes to go, missed sitters.
Bad luck also played a role: Jugovic hit the bar with a 20-metre shot while Beghetto also cleared a Nicola Amoruso header off his own line.
"You have to say that for an hour we were the better side," said Lippi, currently negotiating a new contract with Juventus.
Bologna manager Renzo Ulivieri celebrated the offer of a new four-year contract by watching his side defeat Sampdoria, the club he used to coach, 2-1.

Davide Fontolan, with a goal 20 seconds into the second half, and Russian Igor Shalimov, with a remarkable 30-metre drive, scored Bologna's goals. But the home side also had goalkeeper Francesco Antonioli to thank for victory.

The former AC Milan keeper pulled off inspired first-half saves from Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Jacopino, although Bologna's cause was also aided by the 82nd-minute dismissal of French midfielder Christian Karembeu -- for kicking Shalimov.
Enrico Chiesa, dropped from the Italian World Cup side which beat Giorgia last week, scored Parma's winner in a fine 1-0 victory at Cagliari.
Chiesa's third goal of the season combined breathtaking pace with lethal finishing -- a low precise shot from 20 metres which left Swiss goalkeeper Marco Pascolo helpless.
Parma's ability to dominate Cagliari on their home ground will also take the pressure off manager Carlo Ancelotti.
The job of Ancelotti, at 37 the youngest serie A coach, looked under threat after Parma's early elimination from the Italian Cup and UEFA Cup.
Perugia coach Giovanni Galeone's decision to take his side into a weeklong training retreat after third division Nocerina knocked them out of the Italian Cup paid off with a 3-1 win over Atalanta.
Alberto Di Chiara, Federico Giunti and Massimiliano Allegri scored the goals which brought Perugia their first win since the opening day of the season and halted a run of three defeats.
Oliver Bierhoff, hero of Germany's European championship triumph, struck a late equaliser for Udinese at Napoli before getting sent off for a foul on Brazilian sweeper Andre Cruz.
